newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia car boss dies in helicopter crash.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia car boss dies in helicopter crash.

text.p: Yahaya Ahmad, head Malaysia's national carmaker Proton, was buried on Tuesday after a fiery helicopter crash that also claimed the life of his wife and a pilot.
Yahaya, 50, his wife Rohana Othman, 48, and the pilot died on Monday night in the crash near Kuala Lipis, about 250 km (155 miles) from Kuala Lumpur, a statement from Yahaya's DRB-Hicom Group said.

Yahaya's Proton Bhd makes the ubiquitous Malaysian family saloon. The bespectacled, slight-framed automotive engineer, dubbed the "car czar" in Malaysia, virtually controlled the domestic transport business through DRB-Hicom.
He grabbed international headlines last year when he bought British sports car maker Group Lotus Ltd for 51 million sterling ($83 million).

Photos showed blackened debris of the craft, which went down in a rubber estate in eastern Pahang state. The charred remains of the three helicopter occupants were found under the wreckage, the national Bernama news agency reported.
Yahaya and his wife had been on their way to visit Yahaya's sick mother in adjoining Terengganu state, where Yahaya grew up. They were both buried on Tuesday afternoon in Marang, Terengganu.

Among those at the funeral were Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, who had hand-picked Yahaya to revamp Proton. Scores of other corporate and government officials also were present. The couple had two daughters and two sons.
Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik told reporters in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday that the cause of the crash was still being investigated.

"We haven't got any good indication as yet" on the cause, Ling said in answer to reporters' queries. He said the Department of Civil Aviation (DCA) was heading the probe and that the findings would be submitted to the government.
Meanwhile, the director-general of the DCA said the investigation may take a week, Bernama reported.

The accident was the second aviation mishap in Malaysia in as many days. On Sunday, two cameramen filming a cycling tournament in the northern island of Langkawi were killed along with a pilot when their Cessna 172 light plane nosedived into a mangrove swamp.
Ling, asked if there was a need to step up the regulation of aircraft, said he did not believe this was urgent. "I think we will have to look at it from one year to one year."
Trading in nine of Yahaya's company stocks was suspended on Tuesday after news of his death.
